tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The connected sitectrl account: email, plan status, free-site slot, and credit balance.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the user's sitectrl sites with their live URLs and hosting platform.

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: Details for one site: live URL, draft URL, status.

tools.name: create_site

tools.description: Check whether a site started by create_site has finished. Signed in: pass the slug create_site returned (status building / built / failed). tools.name: edit_site
tools.description: Ask sitectrl's AI editor to change an existing site ('add a contact page', 'make the hero darker'). Edits land in the site's draft; the first build of a brand-new site goes straight live. Returns what changed plus the draft URL.

tools.name: write_site_files
tools.description: Call get_site_context first. Push NEW files (HTML/CSS/JS/images) into a site's DRAFT. To CHANGE an existing page use patch_site_file instead (find/replace on the current file) — rewriting a whole page from memory drops or duplicates things; overwriting an existing .html needs base_hash from read_sit

tools.name: list_site_files
tools.description: List the files in a site's draft tree (paths + sizes).

tools.name: get_site_context
tools.description: CALL THIS BEFORE ANY WRITE. Returns what sitectrl's own editing agent knows about the site: its notes, brand tokens, page inventory, declared invariants, the platform-owned parts every page must keep (with the exact snippet and why), each HTML file's base_hash, and the edit rules (patch, never regen

tools.name: patch_site_file
tools.description: Call get_site_context first. Change an existing draft file IN PLACE — the way to modify a page. Each edit is {find, replace} (swap exact text) or {after, insert} (add text right after an anchor); the anchor must appear exactly once in the current file, else nothing is written and you are told why. tools.name: read_site_file
tools.description: Read one file from a site's draft tree (text, or base64 for binary; 512 KB cap). Returns a 'hash' of the current bytes.

tools.name: publish_site
tools.description: Publish the site's draft to the LIVE site (hosted sites). A snapshot of the previous live version is taken first, so it's undoable.

tools.name: add_component
tools.description: Insert a component from the site's shared library into one or more existing pages, INSTEAD of hand-writing the markup yourself — the classes are already styled and themed to this site's colours. Choices: sc-page-title (the page's one <h1>), sc-gallery (cross-fading photo reel — needs 'images'), sc-i

tools.name: search_domains
tools.description: Search real domain availability + prices (com/net/org/co/io/site and more). Available results include a purchase_url — hand it to the USER to complete checkout; the connector never spends money. Purchased domains connect to their sites in one click.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: The site's private first-party traffic: pageviews/visitors/sessions/clicks totals, top pages, referrers, devices. Windows: 24h, 7d, 30d.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_sites, get_site, get_site_context · Private data: edit_site, write_site_files, list_site_files, get_site_context, patch_site_file, read_site_file, get_analytics · Public sink: whoami, write_site_files, publish_site · Destructive: patch_site_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_sites, get_site, get_site_context · Private data: edit_site, write_site_files, list_site_files, get_site_context, patch_site_file, read_site_file, get_analytics · Public sink: whoami, write_site_files, publish_site · Destructive: patch_site_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
